subject: NAs for indirect effect in lavaan fixed.x = F

messages.author: 0dbd3e9a04506bfd
messages.subject: NAs for indirect effect in lavaan fixed.x = F
parts:
Dear community, 

I am currently conducting a mediation analysis in lavaan using the sem() function with bootstrapped CIs (bootstrapping index = 10000). As all variables in my model are observed variables, I defined fixed.x as False, to allow the exogenous variable to be estimated as well. 

"model <- 
'
                      ## a
                      mediator ~ a*predictor 
                      ## b
                      outcome ~ b*mediator 
                      ## c
                      outcome ~ c*predictor
                      ## indirect effect
                      indirect := a * b
                      ## total effect
                      total := c + (a * b)'

model_sem <- sem(model, 
              data = data_study, 
              missing = "fiml", 
              se = "bootstrap",
              bootstrap = 10000,
              fixed.x = F,                
              iseed = 1)"

However, setting fixed.x to false produces missing values for the standard error, z-value, and p-value of parameter estimates (i.e., indirect effect) of my SEM model in lavaan. 
The estimate as well as the confidence interval are printed. The SEM model runs without any warning (e.g., no convergence problem, no variance problem).

Has anyone experienced similar issues with lavaan? 

Best 
Isabelle

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: NAs for indirect effect in lavaan fixed.x = F
parts:
Did you have missing data? If yes, is "Number of successful bootstrap draws" less than 10000, the requested number of bootstrap samples?

If yes, it may be due to this issue:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues/273

You can try the GitHub version of lavaan to see whether it can solve thee problem:

library(remotes)
install_github("yrosseel/lavaan")

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai

messages.subject: Re: NAs for indirect effect in lavaan fixed.x = F
parts:
Dear Isabelle,

For your information, I tried your code with simulated data (see code below) and it seemed to work (although the simulated data might not be representative of your data set). Do you see any differences between your data and the simulated data that might explain the problem?

library(lavaan)

predictor <- rnorm(200)
mediator <- rnorm(200, 0.4*predictor)
outcome <- rnorm(200, (0.4*mediator + 0.3*predictor))

predictor[sample(1:200, 20)] <- NA
mediator[sample(1:200, 20)] <- NA
outcome[sample(1:200, 20)] <- NA

data_study <- as.data.frame(cbind(predictor, mediator, outcome))

model <- '## a
          mediator ~ a*predictor
          ## b
          outcome ~ b*mediator
          ## c
          outcome ~ c*predictor
          ## indirect effect
          indirect := a * b
          ## total effect
          total := c + (a * b)'

model_sem <- sem(model,
              data = data_study,
              missing = "fiml",
              se = "bootstrap",
              bootstrap = 10000,
              fixed.x = F,                
              iseed = 1)

summary(model_sem)    

Best wishes,

Jasper

"model <- 
'
                      ## a

                      outcome ~ b*mediator 
                      ## c
                      outcome ~ c*predictor
                      ## indirect effect
                      indirect := a * b
                      ## total effect
                      total := c + (a * b)'

Has anyone experienced similar issues with lavaan?
